ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system, $\triangle OAB$ is scaled up with the origin $O$ as the center of similarity to obtain $\triangle OCD$. If $B(0, 1)$ and $D(0, 3)$, what is the ratio of the areas of $\triangle OAB$ to $\triangle OCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\triangle OAB$ be enlarged from the origin $O$ to form $\triangle OCD$, where B(0,1), D(0,3),\\
$\therefore OB\colon OD=1\colon 3$\\
$\therefore$ The ratio of the areas of $\triangle OAB$ and $\triangle OCD$ is $\boxed{1\colon 9}$

From the text, B(0,1) and D(0,3), so OB = 1 and OD = 3. Since B corresponds to D under the dilation centered at O, the linear scale factor from triangle OAB to triangle OCD is 3. Use the rule that areas of similar figures scale by the square of the linear scale factor: area(OAB) : area(OCD) = 1^2 : 3^2 = 1 : 9.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: OB and OD are vertical bases on the y-axis, while A and C are corresponding points of a dilation from O. From the text, B(0,1) and D(0,3), so OD is 3 times OB. Because the dilation is centered at O, every corresponding distance from the y-axis/horizontal height also scales by the same factor 3; in particular, the perpendicular distance from A to the y-axis scales to the perpendicular distance from C to the y-axis by 3. Compute areas using base times height: area(OAB) is proportional to OB times the horizontal distance of A from the y-axis, and area(OCD) is proportional to OD times the horizontal distance of C from the y-axis. Both base and height are multiplied by 3, so the larger area is 3 × 3 = 9 times the smaller area. Therefore area(OAB) : area(OCD) = 1 : 9.
